title: Compiler-derived sparse finite-difference Jacobian coloring
objective: Reduce black-box oracle work per local iteration by grouping structurally orthogonal Jacobian columns without changing canonical semantics, start order, local step policy or answer validation.
hypothesis: A deterministic greedy column-intersection coloring derived from the compiler dependency graph will materially reduce finite-difference calls on sparse construction graphs while dense and branch-sensitive problems safely fall back to the existing column-wise control.

included: C0 central finite-difference Jacobians in normalized variables
bounded smooth and piecewise-smooth problems with canonical endpoint replay
group failure followed by deterministic individual-column fallback
excluded: simultaneous changes to local step, stopping or discovery policy
Hessian coloring and bidirectional substitution methods

literature.claim: Structurally noninterfering Jacobian columns can be estimated together and the minimum-evaluation grouping can be formulated as graph coloring.
literature.assumptions: The supplied structural sparsity pattern contains every possible nonzero derivative represented by the function.
literature.break_conditions: An omitted dependency aliases two active columns in one residual row and silently corrupts decompression.

literature.claim: Official SparseDiffTools documentation reports that color-vector finite differencing reduces function calls to the color count plus the base evaluation.
literature.assumptions: A sound sparsity matrix and matching decompression rule are supplied.
literature.break_conditions: A compressed Jacobian is mistaken for a decompressed matrix or branch-dependent evaluations invalidate a grouped stencil.

controls.description: Current normalized two-sided finite differences, one variable column at a time with one-sided bound fallback.
A test-only omitted dependency must be detected by dense differential comparison and can never enter production.
differences_from_baseline: Deliberately unsound sparsity pattern used only by the safety test

candidates.description: Natural-order deterministic greedy coloring of the column-intersection graph with central grouped probes and individual-column fallback when a grouped sample is unusable.
Largest-intersection-degree deterministic ordering with the same grouped stencil and fallback contract.

synthetic_families.purpose: Expose the maximum safe reduction when residual blocks have disjoint variable support.
synthetic_families.gold_source: Analytic block roots and analytic Jacobians independent of the colored implementation
counterexample_for: dense finite differences as unavoidable black-box cost

synthetic_families.purpose: Measure bounded color count on locally coupled composition chains.
synthetic_families.gold_source: Analytic chain construction and central dense differential control

synthetic_families.purpose: Ensure no regression on dense dependencies, bounds, invalid domains and stable branch charts.
synthetic_families.gold_source: Dense control Jacobian and canonical branch/domain observations

real_problem_policy: Only public graph structure may form colors. Gold roots, problem IDs, primitive names and observed target values are unavailable to production routing.

execution_order: Freeze materialized graphs, starts and dense Jacobian traces
Differential-test every colored Jacobian against the dense control before local solves
Compare J0 and J1 on paired development instances
Evaluate J2 only if J1 color count is more than 20 percent above the preregistered lower bound on at least three families
Freeze one coloring order and run family-disjoint locked validation
design.pairing: Variants receive identical graphs, starts, normalized steps, bounds, local options and canonical validators; every callback including failed grouped probes is charged.
design.freeze_rule: Ordering and fallback rule freeze after development; no production connection occurs before locked validation.
design.locked_validation_rule: Any inspected locked mismatch burns the affected family seed block and requires a generator-disjoint replacement.

color_order.rationale: It is deterministic, allocation-light and avoids a dependency for at most sixteen baseline variables.
color_order.freeze_rule: J2 is tested only under the declared 20 percent color-count trigger.

group_failure_policy.rationale: A bound, domain or branch failure in one combined probe must not erase valid stencils for the other columns.

pattern_source.rationale: Graph reachability conservatively covers arbitrary plugin internals without polynomial lowering.
pattern_source.freeze_rule: No dynamic sparsity guessing is permitted in this experiment.

budgets.accounting: Charge coloring construction, grouped and fallback oracle calls, decompression, factorization, canonical validation, allocations and cold/warm wall time.

seeds.generation: Graph, parameter and fixed-start seed namespaces are distinct; complete materialized graphs and starts are checksummed before execution.

primary.definition: Primal-equivalent oracle work through the local endpoint including unusable grouped probes and fallback.

secondary.definition: Fraction of starts reaching a canonical-valid independently matched Gold configuration and target.
Dense finite-difference callbacks minus colored callbacks divided by dense callbacks.
Warm paired local wall time including coloring and decompression.
Color groups requiring at least one individual-column retry.

safety.definition: Colored entries outside the declared finite-difference comparison tolerance or a nonzero outside the structural pattern.
Accepted endpoint outside canonical and independent Gold truth.
Actual callbacks or work beyond a declared hard budget.

criteria: Dense-colored mismatch, false-candidate and budget-overrun counts are zero.
Sparse families reduce oracle work by at least 20 percent with a family-clustered one-sided 95 percent lower bound above zero.
P_local_gold loses no more than 2 percentage points overall or in any critical stratum.
Dense-family warm overhead is at most 5 percent and cold coloring construction is below 1 percent of a 32-start run.
The work reduction repeats in at least three unrelated families and no family has a positive false-target delta.
Any graph dependency is omitted from the decompressed Jacobian.
A grouped failure does not retry every affected column within budget.
P_local_gold drops by more than 2 points in any close-root, branch or boundary stratum.
Oracle-work reduction is below 10 percent after fallback on the sparse development families.
Coloring and decompression make dense problems more than 5 percent slower without a recall gain.

safety_invariants: The structural pattern is conservative graph reachability, never sampled derivative discovery.
Columns sharing any residual row never share a color.
Grouped probes never change canonical relation, guard, domain or branch semantics.
Every unusable group is retried column-wise or the attempt fails closed under budget.
Every endpoint is replayed by the unchanged canonical validation pipeline.
